comments.note: Deduplication logic in checkWorkspaceHealth() correctly uses a seenRepos Set with entries returned newest-first, so only the most recent credential error per repo is surfaced. However, the implementation surfaces the most-recent entry across all runs rather than strictly from the last setup invocation. This is acceptable behavior — if a repo later clones successfully, no new 'credentials' error entry is written and the old entry remains in the log, potentially surfacing a stale badge. This is a pre-existing design constraint of the error-log approach and was acknowledged in the WP notes.

No test covers the dual edge case: credential-missing badge clears from the status table when credentialErrorRepoIds is deleted (i.e. when a repo later receives live status data after successful re-clone). This clearing path is exercised by the pre-existing applyStatusMapUpdate() logic and is already guarded by line 1180-1181 in workspace-detail.js, but has no dedicated regression test. Low risk — the existing logic predates this WP.

comments.note: workspace-health.ts line 83 comment: corrected inaccurate description of deduplication strategy. The original text said 'only repos whose entry is from the most recent setup invocation (i.e. the entry with the highest Id)' — this implies Id-based comparison, which is not how deduplication works. The actual mechanism is Set-based deduplication over entries already returned newest-first by errorLogManager.list(). Updated comment to accurately describe what the code does. No behavior change.

workspace-health.ts Check 3: the credential-missing check fires for ALL error log entries with Source: 'credentials' scoped to the workspace, regardless of whether that error is stale (e.g. repo later successfully cloned on a different machine). This is a known design limitation noted by QA. If a future WP adds a 'credentials OK' success log entry, this check could filter it out. Worth considering for a follow-up work package.

[documentation-forward] workspace-health.ts: the JSDoc for checkWorkspaceHealth() documents the 3 check types accurately, but does not mention the known limitation that credential-missing badges may persist if the error log is never cleared after a successful credential fix. The QA pipeline flagged this as acceptable behavior. A brief 'Known limitation' note in the JSDoc or a code comment near Check 3 would help future contributors understand why stale badges may appear without a new Setup run.
